Louisiana produces the most ammonia from natural gas in the United States, making up approximately 34 percent of capacity (Fernandez, 2024). Much of the ammonia production is clustered in the central and south-central United States, where there is both the biggest natural gas supply and ammonia demand, as fertilizer. Exhibit 1-4. Generally, ammonia prices were relatively volatile during the 2000–2024 period. Starting in 2020, ammonia prices rose significantly, up 170 percent in 2021 and 90 percent in 2022, reaching $1,212/tonne NH in 2022. This was followed by a 56 percent decrease in the price to 3 $529/tonne NH in 2023. The volatility during the 2020–2024 time period correlated with the 3 rise in international natural gas prices and global events such as the COVID-19 pandemic supply chain disruptions, sanctions related to geopolitical conflicts, and export restrictions (EIA, 2022) (Wang, et al., 2023). 10 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION Exhibit 1-5. Nominal U.S. ammonia prices for 2020–2024 (Apodaca, 2025) 1.3 PRODUCTION TECHNOLOGIES Conventional ammonia production requires N and H as inputs. High-purity H is obtained 2 2 2 through conventional H production routes such as natural gas reforming and coal gasification. 2 N is sourced by using air directly or from a N generator or air separation unit (ASU). H and N 2 2 2 2 are mixed, and the comingled stream is compressed to 120–220 bar (1,700–3,200 psi) before entering the Haber-Bosch synthesis loop (EPA, 1993). The NH synthesis reactor operates at a 3 temperature of 380–520 °C and typically contains an iron catalyst promoted with potassium oxide and aluminum oxide (EPA, 1993). The Haber-Bosch process, represented by the equilibrium reaction , typically achieves a single-pass conversion of 20–30 percent (EPA, 1993), influenced significantly by operating pressure, temperature, and the N2 +3H2 ↔ 2NH3 specific activity of the iron-based catalyst. Therefore, the continual recycling of unreacted reagents is needed to achieve an overall conversion of more than 98 percent. The final step is refrigeration in which the ammonia stream is reduced to a temperature ranging -10 to -25 °C for separation of unconverted gases, which are recycled, and also for product storage. In the reforming process, syngas, comprising primarily H and CO, is produced by reforming 2 natural gas and undergoes water gas shift in which additional H and CO is produced. Next, the 2 2 CO in the shifted syngas is removed via an acid gas removal unit, such as a solvent-based CO 2 2 capture system (Bartels, 2008).
